<h2>Build research depth over time.</h2>
<p>Students interested in sustainability research can start with faculty-led projects, short-term working groups, lab meetings, and methods training, then move toward independent projects, conference presentations, and graduate-school preparation.</p>

## Ways to Start

::: {.student-card-grid}

::: {.student-card}
### Join a research lab

Labs such as PRISE give students exposure to data collection, literature review, coding, research design, and applied policy questions. You do not need every possible activity; sustained work in one serious research setting is often more valuable than a long list of shallow experiences.
:::

::: {.student-card}
### Build technical skills

Start learning R, Python, statistics, and quantitative methods through UTD-supported resources such as Coursera or DataCamp, and through courses that require original research papers, data analysis, or applied policy projects.
:::

::: {.student-card}
### Work with faculty

Use [Research Explorer](https://profiles.utdallas.edu/){target="_blank"} to find faculty whose interests match yours. Reach out with a concise note explaining the research topic, your skills, and what kind of assistance you can provide.
:::

::: {.student-card}
### Present your work

By junior year, aim to present posters or papers, apply to conferences, and build a CV that shows depth. Publications are helpful when feasible, but consistent research experience and strong faculty recommendations also matter.
:::

:::

## UTD Research Pathways

- [Undergraduate Research Apprenticeship Program (URAP)](https://honors.utdallas.edu/research/undergraduate-research-apprenticeship-program/){target="_blank"} connects students with faculty-led research.
- [SPUR](https://spur.utdallas.edu/){target="_blank"} supports student posters and undergraduate research presentation.
- [Undergraduate Research Scholar Awards (URSA)](https://oue.utdallas.edu/research/undergraduate-research-scholar-awards/){target="_blank"} provide funding for independent research.
- [Clark Summer Research Program](https://honors.utdallas.edu/research/clark-program/){target="_blank"} supports summer research experience.
- [UTD research facilities and centers](https://www.utdallas.edu/research/facilities-centers/){target="_blank"} can help students identify labs, centers, and applied research communities beyond their home department.

## Year-by-Year Guide

::: {.year-plan}

::: {.year-step}
### First year

Take stronger math and methods courses, start learning R or Python, attend lab meetings or policy seminars, and identify faculty whose work matches your interests. The goal is to build basic research skills and find a research environment you can stay with.
:::

::: {.year-step}
### Sophomore year

Move deeper into faculty-led research, take higher-level theory or methods courses, and apply for programs such as URSA, URAP, the Clark Summer Research Program, or external summer research fellowships. The goal is technical growth and broader exposure.
:::

::: {.year-step}
### Junior year

Start leading a bounded independent project or work closely with faculty on a coauthored project. Apply to present at conferences, build a poster or paper, and identify faculty who can write detailed recommendations about your research skills.
:::

::: {.year-step}
### Senior year

Complete a senior thesis or capstone project when appropriate, clarify your research niche, and use your strongest projects to write graduate-school or fellowship applications. If you are considering applied economics PhD programs, check math requirements early.
:::

:::

## Sustainability Topics at PRISE

Students can build research experience around questions such as:

- environmental shocks, political accountability, and climate policy;
- conservation program effectiveness and tropical forest loss;
- clean energy adoption and household welfare;
- pollution exposure, water quality, and environmental inequality;
- remote sensing, survey data, and causal inference for applied policy.

Current lab openings are listed on the [Get Involved](get-involved.qmd) page.
